newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GUZMAN, BLUE JAYS BLANK WHITE SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GUZMAN, BLUE JAYS BLANK WHITE SOX.

text.p: Juan Guzman and three relievers combined on a four-hitter Thursday as the Toronto Blue Jays recorded their second straight shutout over the Chicago White Sox, 4-0.

Guzman (2-0) allowed three hits and four walks with three strikeouts in seven innings. The 1996 American League earned run average champ, who gave up just one run and two hits over seven innings against Milwaukee on Friday, lowered his ERA to 0.64 so far this season.

"I'm 2-0 and I'm feeling pretty good," said Guzman, who has a streak of 13 consecutive scoreless innings. "It's nice getting runs. That was a problem for me last year. I just hope and pray that I'll have more run support than last year."
Dan Plesac retired the first two batters of the eighth and Tim Crabtree got Frank Thomas to fly out to end the inning. Mike Timlin allowed a hit and a walk in the ninth, but closed out the shutout.
"We threw two pretty good pitchers at them," said Toronto manager Cito Gaston. "Guzman and Roger (Clemens) made it tough on them. The weather had an effect, but you have to give the pitchers credit.
Playing in chilly conditions, Chicago's number three through five hitters -- Thomas, Albert Belle and Harold Baines -- combined to go 0-for-11 in the game and 1-for-21 in the two games.
"Those guys are good hitters and once the weather gets warmer, they will heat up," said Gaston.

With one out in the second, Ed Sprague walked, Carlos Delgado singled and Benito Santiago walked to load the bases against James Baldwin (0-1). Shawn Green then walked to force home a run and a wild pitch allowed Delgado to come home and make it 2-0.

In the ninth, against Tony Castillo, Sprague doubled and Santiago reached base one out later on third baseman Chris Snopek's throwing error. Pinch-hitter Robert Perez then doubled in a run and, after Alex Gonzalez was intentionally walked, Otis Nixon drew a walk to extend the margin to 4-0.

In Milwaukee, Bobby Witt allowed just three hits in eight innings in his first start of the year and Mark McLemore and Ivan Rodriguez each had fifth-inning RBI singles as the Texas Rangers defeated the Brewers 2-0.
Only 5,638 were in attendance for Milwaukee's second home game of the season. Cold weather had postponed a game between the teams on Wednesday and it was nearly as chilly Thursday.
"Witt threw extremely well," said Rangers manager Johnny Oates. "It was a good day for a power pitcher. He made a lot of quality pitches and pitched ahead most of the day."

Milwaukee had no extra-base hits off Witt (1-0), who walked one and struck out five. Fernando Vina and Dave Nilsson each had singles in the fourth inning and Marc Newfield added a single in the seventh for the Brewers' only hits.
"Throughout the whole day, I was just trying to get ahead and throw strikes," said Witt.

"It seemed like both sides were up there swinging today, taking aggressive hacks and any time that happens, you just try to throw strikes and hopefully they'll put the ball in play and things worked out well today."
John Wetteland, who signed a four-year, $23 million free agent contract in the off-season, worked a hitless ninth for his first save as a Ranger.
Milwaukee had a runner reach second base just once, in the fourth.
Milwaukee starter Scott Karl (0-2) took the loss.
In Detroit, Paul Molitor had four hits and drove in a pair of runs including the go-ahead single in the fourth inning, as the Minnesota Twins cruised to a 7-3 victory over the Tigers.
The Twins averted a three-game sweep and finally held down the Detroit offence, which scored 20 runs in the first two games. Detroit had won four of its previous five games.

Rich Robertson was expected to start for the Twins, but was a late scratch due to the flu. Former Tiger Scott Aldred (1-0) took his place and allowed three runs and four hits with three walks in five innings to get the win.
Mike Trombley allowed a hit and a walk with four strikeouts in three innings and Rick Aguilera worked the ninth.
Willie Blair (0-2) took the loss.

In Kansas City, the game between the Baltimore Orioles and Royals was postponed due to rain and cold, just one degree above freezing. It will be made up as part of a doubleheader at Kauffman Stadium on August 19.
